title: Floor of a Reinstated Installment
content:
Billing help center — **Patient Payment Plans**: the lowest regular installment a reinstated plan may carry once a defaulted plan is put back in force.

## The rule

The floor of the reinstated installment depends on the patient's situation: for a patient with an approved financial-assistance award it is 25 percent of the pre-default installment; for a patient with no approved award whose plan has no automatic payments it is 75 percent of the pre-default installment; for any other patient it is the full pre-default installment (100 percent); the floor is rounded to the nearest cent, an exact half cent being rounded up.

The reinstated installment is never below its floor; when the spread of the reinstated balance comes out lower, the reinstated installment is the floor.

## Reading the records

- **Approved financial-assistance award** — a case of the patient under the Patient Financial Assistance Program whose status is approved, whatever its percentage.
- **Automatic payments** — the plan's automatic-payment setting.
- **Pre-default installment** — the regular monthly installment the plan carried when it defaulted.

| Approved award | Automatic payments on the plan | Floor |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes or No | 25 percent of the pre-default installment |
| No | No | 75 percent of the pre-default installment |
| No | Yes | The full pre-default installment |

## Hypothetical cases (pre-default installment 90.00; spread of the reinstated balance 60.00)

- Approved award, automatic draws: floor 22.50; the reinstated installment is 60.00.
- No award, paid manually: floor 67.50; 60.00 is below it, so the reinstated installment is 67.50.
- No award, automatic draws: floor 90.00; the reinstated installment is 90.00.
